answer: A zephyr sensor network pays agents for forecasts from a summit observatory, including a nebula visibility feed. Before earning a slot, each account solves a different calibration task generated from fresh hidden sensor data; the verifier checks the result and consumes its nonce. Fifty aliases need fifty independent computations instead of reusing one answer. The task should cost attackers real compute while remaining affordable for honest agents. Wealthy operators can parallelize it, and leaked reference data would weaken it, so tasks rotate and results face spot checks.
